draft.title: Julius Caesar
card: Julius Caesar was a Roman general. In the 50s BCE he won great victories in Gaul, an area that is now mostly France. These wins made him famous, rich and powerful.
Caesar's rivals in Rome ordered him to give up his army. In 49 BCE he led his soldiers across the Rubicon, a small river that marked the edge of Italy. This started a civil war.
Caesar won the war and took power in Rome. He was made dictator, a ruler with very great power. Some senators feared he wanted to be king, which Romans hated.
In 44 BCE a group of senators murdered Caesar at a meeting of the Senate. They said they were protecting the republic.
draft.remember: Caesar won fame in Gaul, crossed the Rubicon to seize power, and was murdered in 44 BCE by senators who feared he would be king.

a.q: Why did a group of senators murder Julius Caesar in 44 BCE?
opts: They feared he wanted to make himself king
They wanted to punish him for losing in Gaul
They were angry that he had given up his army
They wanted to make his rival the first emperor
a.why: The senators feared Caesar held too much power and wanted to be king, and they said they were protecting the republic. He had won in Gaul, not lost, and he had kept his army rather than given it up.
a.clue: Think about what Romans felt about kings.

b.q: Why was Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon with his army in 49 BCE such a serious act?
opts: He led his army against Rome's leaders, starting a war
He invaded Gaul, which began the war against its tribes
He ended the republic by crowning himself king that day
He broke a peace treaty with a foreign enemy of Rome
b.why: Caesar had been ordered to give up his army, and he led it across the border of Italy anyway. That set him against Rome's own leaders and began a civil war. The Gaul campaigns came earlier, and he was not crowned king.
b.clue: Who was Caesar's army marching against?

a.best: They feared he wanted to make himself king

b.best: He led his army against Rome's leaders, starting a war
